answer: A memory-latency attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to traverse an intertwined vine of pointer lookups in physical DRAM. An attacker incurs dedicated memory-bus bandwidth per identity, teetering on a costly hardware ledge as expenses scale linearly. Honest agents bend like a willow under load bursts by deferring non-critical proofs. However, adversaries using ASICs with on-chip SRAM can bypass latency bottlenecks, significantly reducing verification costs.
